units.en: Leina's servant, who can transform into three forms: robot, jet helicopter and supercar. Technically a member of the Jet tribe. Because Triple Jim can carry members of the Cronos tribe, Jim is a great help when traveling, but is poor at fighting because of a gentle nature. That said, Jim understands how martial artists feel, and often put Jim's own body on the line for Leina's sake. Always humble and polite in speech, Jim shouts "It is above you, if you please!" even when warning someone that something is falling from above. In episode 24, Jim performed a catchphrase imitating Rom's. Jim also seems to be able to use Tenku Chushin Ken, though only a little.
units.notes: Gender of Triple Jim is unknown in the glossary, so no gendered pronouns are used.
uncertain: Gender unknown: 'Jim' repeated instead of a pronoun.
The line shouted ('above, if you please') is a paraphrase of the polite 'ue de gozaimasu'.

units.name_jp: トリプル・ジム・スーパーカー
units.en: Triple Jim's supercar form. In the original story, Triple Jim usually carried Leina in this form when they traveled. Incidentally, Rom rode a machine called Flex.
uncertain: 'Flex' = Battle Flex on English Wikipedia (Rom's jeep).

units.name_jp: トリプル・ジム・ヘリ
units.en: Triple Jim's jet helicopter form. In an emergency, Triple Jim makes high-speed trips in this form.

units.name_jp: パワーライザー（レイナ）
units.en: Reinforced armor for the Cronos tribe, built by Wrestler Robo for Rom after Kenro was taken from him. According to Rom, it is "a magnificent design with absolutely no waste." The arms and legs are linked to the wearer's brain waves, so the wearer can move them at will, as if they were the wearer's own body. However, because it is controlled by brain waves, it has the weakness that it becomes uncontrollable if the wearer's anger is too intense, and the arms and legs stop moving entirely if the wearer freezes in fear. It can also dash at high speed using rollers and fly for short periods using thrusters, and Rom used this Power Riser to perform Tenku Chushin Ken techniques.
units.notes: The library text describes Rom's use of the Power Riser; the entry itself is the Leina variant.
uncertain: 'Wrestler Robo' is a literal translation of the kana (no English source).
Who took Kenro is not stated in this entry (Garudi in the series).

units.en: A warrior of the Jet tribe who, like Rom and Drill, trained under Kirai. He was taught Tenku Shin Ken by Kirai. As his name suggests, he can transform into a jet aircraft. Within Rom's party he is the cool, handsome type, who dashes in to rescue friends and beautiful women in their moment of crisis. He is also quite sharp, and often served as Rom's strategist. His only built-in weapon is the sword stored at his waist, from which he unleashes various secret techniques of Tenku Shin Ken. The Blazer Cannon is an additional weapon that appeared from the middle of the original story; it has the same name as Rod Drill's, but the cannon on Jet fires beams.

units.name_jp: ブルー・ジェット（変形）
units.en: Blue Jet's flight form. In exchange for losing the use of his sword, Vulcans and the Blazer Cannon become usable as built-in weapons. In the original story, he also sometimes traveled with Rom hanging from him. Incidentally, the shout of "Je-e-et!" when transforming into this form was first thought up by Blue Jet and became popular among the Jet tribe.

A fellow disciple of Rom and Jet. He is from the Battle tribe and transforms into a drill tank. Cheerful and bold, he excels at power-based fighting. He was something of a mood maker within the party, yet repeatedly saved his companions from danger with that drill. He is the type who sleeps a full 10 hours, and apparently once punched Jet in his sleep when Jet came to wake him. He has no built-in weapons, and since his trademark drill cannot be used in this form either, he fights with his fists alone, but he rarely shouts technique names; the only one confirmed is "Tenku Chushin Ken: Head-Hunting." The Blazer Cannon differs from Jet's in the shape of its muzzle, and is a missile launcher.
uncertain: 'Tenku Chushin Ken: Head-Hunting' is my translation of the technique name (no English source).
'Fellow disciple' for the kana 'brother disciple'.

units.en: Rod Drill's drill tank form. With drill charges and Vulcans, it has more armament than the humanoid form, and it can burrow underground. For some reason, Drill seems to be afraid of spiders and long, thin things (Cronos earthworms). In addition, Drill is used to handling explosives and is surprisingly an artist, making him a rather mysterious character.
uncertain: 'Drill charges' is the translation of the plain word 'drill assault' ([jp]); could also be 'charges with the drill'.

units.en: A medium-sized robot that Rom merges with. Its name is written with the characters for "sword" and "dragon." When the energy of light reaches its peak, Kenro crosses the dimensional wall and summons Kenryu. By merging with Kenryu, Rom is able to display tens of times his usual strength. Kenryu often fights using Kenro, and, like Tenku Chushin Ken, makes frequent use of Tenku Shin Ken.

A giant robot that Rom merges into, from Kenryu. Its name is written with the characters for "double" and "kung fu." The merge into Baikanfu is specifically called the Pile Formation. When Kenro, receiving Rom's will, turns to light in midair, the Pile Formation is completed, transcending time and dimensions. Baikanfu synchronizes with all the energy on the earth's surface and can produce power capable of changing even natural phenomena. It makes relatively frequent use of electric-type techniques such as Lightning Smash and Thunder Punch, but it has many other techniques as well, each carrying one-hit-kill destructive power. The shield used by Kenryu can, like Kenro, also be used in the Baikanfu state.
uncertain: 'All the energy on the earth's surface' ([jp]) could also mean 'all the energy on the ground'.
'Pile Formation' is a translation of the katakana (no English source).

units.en: A mass-production Dragonar. A main weapon of the Earth Alliance Forces, built at the secret weapons factory in Chongqing by making use of the combat data of the D-Weapons. Equipped with an excellent auto-sensor, it has, on paper, the combined capabilities of three machines: Dragonar-1, Dragonar-2 and Dragonar-3. Although it was given what, when you think about it, is only natural for a mass-production machine (specs superior to the prototypes), for the sake of the story it ended up as nothing more than a mecha that exists to be beaten.
uncertain: 'Earth Alliance Forces' follows the game's wording ([jp]); the official Sunrise site says 'Earth Federation'.

units.en: A prototype Metal Armor developed as a close-combat unit with excellent mobility, called by the abbreviation "D-1." Metal Armor is the general term for the humanoid mobile weapons developed by the Giganos Empire, and it developed from lunar work robots called Metal Workers. As this suggests, the Dragonars were made in Giganos but were seized by the Earth Alliance, and the three units together are also called the "D-Weapons." For the Earth Alliance, which lacks Metal Armor development technology, the D-Weapons are trump-card machines for turning the tide. The main armament is a 75 mm hand rail gun and close-combat laser swords mounted on both hips; the two laser swords can be joined to make a twin sword. Both shoulders also carry grenades called shoulder bombs. By being fitted with Lifter-1, a flight unit for atmospheric flight, the D-1, which already boasted high combat power, gained mobility and was powered up further. Incidentally, the D-1's computer is nicknamed Clara.

units.name_jp: ドラグナー１型カスタム
units.en: A D-1 that underwent reinforcement modifications at the hands of Dr. Plato. By incorporating know-how gained from developing the Dragoon and the Alliance's own technology, its mid-range combat and search-and-detection abilities have been improved, and its original close-combat ability has also been powered up. The two laser swords are mounted on the left hip, and a throw-in bomb is equipped on the right hip. Also, because a gravity field detection system was installed on the left shoulder, the shoulder bombs have been reduced to a single one on the right shoulder.
uncertain: 'Throw-in bomb' ([jp]) is a literal rendering of the kana; no English source.

units.en: A prototype Metal Armor developed for long-range support. Abbreviated "D-2." Its main armament is the 280 mm rail cannons on both shoulders, which alone have enough firepower to smash an enemy in one hit, and it also has a wealth of optional equipment such as twin Gatling cannons and rocket launchers, making it an extremely heavily armed machine. It does carry an assault knife for close combat, but it is poor at close-range fighting. The D-2's flight unit, Lifter-2, has a refueling system and can also refuel the other two machines. Incidentally, the D-2's computer is nicknamed Sonia.

units.name_jp: ドラグナー２型カスタム
units.en: A reinforced and modified D-2. Unlike the D-1 Custom, which raised overall performance, the modification focused on raising firepower, the D-2's greatest feature. The rail cannons on both shoulders have become a large 640 mm caliber, and the twin automatic cannons that were omitted when the Lifter is worn have been revived. In addition, twin heavy dual missiles have been newly added to the legs. Naturally, armor and generator output have also been increased.

A prototype Metal Armor developed for electronic warfare. With excellent reconnaissance, detection and intelligence-gathering abilities, it supports the combat operations of the D-1 and D-2 and disrupts the enemy. It can also hack enemy base computers and neutralize enemy holograms, so its field of activity is broad. However, since it is not a combat machine, its armor and armament are kept to a minimum, and various sensors and radars are embedded in their place. Lifter-3, the flight unit for the D-3, is likewise a lightweight type that emphasizes speed, and the D-3 has the highest speed of the three machines. Incidentally, the D-3's computer is nicknamed Maggie.

The D-3 shows no change in outward appearance, but its electronic warfare equipment has been updated in both software and hardware. Armor and thrust have also been improved, so it can be said that it has effectively become a custom model.

A defensive fighter owned by Daimobic. Its pilots are Kyoshiro Yuzuki and Nana Izumi, and its main mission is supporting Daimos. It has two Vulcans behind the cockpit and missiles under the main wings, and sometimes fired beams from the antenna-like part on its nose. Its combat power is surprisingly high, and it saved Daimos from danger many times. Of course, it can also operate in space. Also, perhaps because its pilot Kyoshiro is skilled, it showed considerable maneuverability and dodged enemy attacks over and over, and was almost never shot down. For that reason it gives a very sleek impression compared with Daimos, which is always covered in scars.

A super robot built through the cooperation of Dr. Ryuzaki and Dr. Izumi. It was originally a trailer for underground development that was converted into a combat robot, and uses Daimolite as its energy source. Daimolite is crystallized light born from a neutrino reaction; the light particles solidified under high gravity collide violently with one another and thereby keep emitting enormous energy. Also, Daimolite triggers a nuclear reaction and explodes massively at 4 degrees Celsius or above, and when fully released, it turns Daimos itself into a pure energy body. Because Daimos has a control system that traces the pilot's movements, it reproduces Kazuya's karate techniques without the slightest error, but conversely it has the weakness that when Daimos takes damage, the pilot takes damage too. Its weapons are mostly mid- and close-range ones such as the Five Shooter and the Triple Dragon Staff, making it a machine that emphasizes close combat. Also, the "Deadly Gale Correct Fist Thrust" was originally not a combination technique with Blizzard-type weapons but the name of the karate technique itself that delivers the finishing blow; likewise, following up from Blizzard-type weapons, it also used the "Deadly Gale Hand-Blade Thrust" and the "Deadly Daimos Chop."
uncertain: '4 degrees Celsius or above' is as written in the source (it looks odd but is the original figure).
Technique names are translated from the Japanese; see glossary weapons for the SRW wiki basis.

units.en: An all-purpose fighter owned by Mutropolis. It was used for many purposes, including not only combat but also reconnaissance, investigation and rescue operations. In the original story, it has a crew of three, and the upper part of the cockpit is a small aircraft, the Spit Fighter, which also serves as an escape device.
uncertain: 'Spit Fighter' ([jp]) is a literal rendering of the kana.

units.en: A mystical super robot built through the science of the ancient Mu Empire 12,000 years ago. Normally it is stored in a golden base-body state inside Divine Face Rock, and it starts moving when Akira climbs into it (fade-in). It uses the mysterious energy Mutron, and the Mutron metal used in its armor exhibits self-repair ability by returning to the base-body state. There are also many parts of its interior that remain unexplained, and in the latter half of the original story it showed its true power through a Mutron energy release device called the Star of Ra Mu. Its main finishing move is God Bird, in which it transforms into a bird form and charges at Mach 7. Raideen can be piloted only by Akira, who carries the blood of Ra Mu, emperor of the Mu Empire, and its control method is a unique one that is integrated with Akira's body movements.
uncertain: 'Divine Face Rock' ([jp]): ja Wikipedia writes [jp] (Human-Face Rock); kept the game's wording.

units.en: Raideen's bird-shaped flight form, mainly used when traveling long distances. It also takes this form when using the finishing move "God Bird," in which it sets its aim on an opponent's weak point and charges. There is much about its internal structure that is unknown, and from the middle of the story onward it comes to use a brutal technique called Head Cutter.

A powerful commander who once even took the No. 1 spot in the Gyandlar Commander ranking, in place of Devil Saturn 6. Asura fires Nattoru bullets, which rob the target of bodily freedom, from the abdomen, and specializes in destroying the immobilized opponent in cruel ways. By nature Asura is cruel and cunning, and once set a trap by turning Rom's party's surprise attack plan against them. Asura drove Baikanfu into a corner, but was pierced through the chest by Thunder Cyclone and defeated.
units.notes: Library entry 157; the batch label was the placeholder 'none' (unit-table name Asura, kana Ashura).
uncertain: Gender of Asura unknown: no pronouns used.
'Nattoru bullet' is romanized from kana (no English source).

units.en: The boss of the space crime organization Gyandlar. Gyandlar's goal is to rule the entire universe and bring darkness and fear. It is also searching for Hyribead, an infinite energy said to grant eternal life. Gadess is a villain who has wandered space for thousands of years piling up evil deeds, and trusts no one but himself. His sorcerous power is such that he can paralyze enemies in distant places. He attacked planet Cronos after Hyribead, but his ambition was thwarted by the Cronos tribe warriors, including Rom. He hates having rust form on his body to an extreme degree, and always kept with him a dedicated robot, Bibibi Mouse, to polish his body.
units.notes: Batch label was 'Gades' (kana [jp]) with series Machine Robo: correct.
uncertain: Gender male per ja Wikipedia/voice actors (glossary).
'Bibibi Mouse' romanized from kana.

units.en: A low-ranking Gyandlar Commander. When first introduced, Casmodon appeared as the main enemy and tried to set the Cronos tribe and the Battle tribe against each other, but after that appeared in large numbers as a grunt. Casmodon can transform into a flight form like a jet aircraft.
uncertain: Gender unknown: 'Casmodon' repeated.

units.en: One of the Gyandlar executives. Fond of underhanded schemes and plots, Grujios serves as a kind of strategist for Gyandlar. With tremendous sorcerous power, Grujios can revive the ghosts of Gyandlar Commanders and use them as servants. In truth, the real body is only a caterpillar-like face floating in the tank of the head. Grujios was defeated by Rom in the Battle of the Heavenly Demon Castle, but, just as promised in the "I shall return" warning, came back in spirit form. After becoming a spirit, Grujios gained a new ability to take over other people's bodies, and tormented Rom's party by posing as an ally.
uncertain: Gender unknown: no pronouns used.
'Battle of the Heavenly Demon Castle' is my translation of the event name.

units.en: A low-ranking Gyandlar Commander. Zarios is characterized by caterpillar-track legs, but had no especially notable role in the original story.

A female Gyandlar executive. In contrast to Grujios, so to speak, she often takes direct command at the front lines. Devil Saturn 6 are her direct subordinates. Wielding an electromagnetic whip, her speech and attitude fit being called "Big Sis," but she gets angry when called that. She is bold and cruel by nature, and tries to compete with Grujios at every turn. She also has a cute side in that she is actually afraid of earthquakes, and in the original story she almost got on good terms with Tough Trailer for a moment. After that, she set a trap for Tough Trailer by making that character hold the Medusa demon sword, a cursed blade that drives its holder mad, but after that scheme failed, she herself came to favor the Medusa demon sword. She can also breathe fire from her mouth and emit hypnotic light from her eyes.
uncertain: Tough Trailer's gender is not sourced, so no pronoun is used for that character.
'Big Sis' for the nickname Aneego (boss-lady / older-sister).

units.en: The combined form of Devil Saturn No. 1 through No. 6. Thanks to its viciousness and power it has held the No. 1 spot in the Gyandlar Commander ranking; it dropped in rank once, but soon came back. Its attacks are varied: not only fighting, but also flames from the mouth, claws launched on chains, beams from the eyes, and so on. It once even devised the Devil Foot Smash to counter God Hand Smash. It was often entrusted with Gyandlar's field operations, and was beaten up by Rom and the others time after time. It is a commander whose odd Kansai dialect makes it hard to hate, but in fact only Devil Saturn No. 1 actually uses the Kansai dialect, and the other five speak standard Japanese.
uncertain: 'Devil Saturn' vs. English Wikipedia 'Devil Satan'.
'God Hand Smash' is a translation of the kana (Rom/Baikanfu technique).

units.en: A low-ranking Gyandlar Commander. Its agility is its trait, but it seems not to have been depicted much in the original story.

An artificial weather satellite developed by Diondra. Phenomena No. 1 can not only generate thunderclouds artificially, but also make lightning strike a targeted location by laser guidance. The lightning has a terrifying power: a voltage of 10,000 volts and a temperature of over 30,000 degrees. Phenomena No. 2, developed later, was planned to disturb the geomagnetism of planet Cronos, destroy the ozone layer overhead, and make electromagnetic waves that drive Machine Robo mad rain down onto the surface, but through an unexpected accident it caused a pole shift on planet Cronos.
uncertain: Voltage figure is as written (10,000 V) although it looks low for lightning.

units.en: The fifth Angel confirmed. It has a regular octahedral exterior and attacks approaching enemies with a powerful charged particle cannon. To defeat this Angel, NERV used a hastily built modified positron cannon for EVAs (NERV spec) and carried out Operation Yashima, supplying it with electric power from all over Japan.
units.notes: Library entry 166; batch label was '[jp]' (name from the unit table: [jp]). Cross-series (Evangelion).

units.en: The thirteenth Angel confirmed. Hiding inside a cumulonimbus cloud, it came into contact with Evangelion Unit-03, which was being transported to NERV's Second Experimental Site in Matsushiro, and completely took over Unit-03, which had just finished an activation test with Toji still aboard, and was designated an Angel. It went as far as defeating Unit-00 and Unit-02, but was destroyed by Unit-01, which had activated the Dummy System.
units.notes: Library entry 167; cross-series (Evangelion).

units.en: The fourteenth Angel confirmed. It invaded the Geofront from Third New Tokyo City and, with overwhelming attack power beyond that of any previous Angel, defeated Unit-02 and Unit-00. In the end it fought the berserk Unit-01 and was devoured.
units.notes: Library entry 168; cross-series (Evangelion).

units.en: The Fifth Child dispatched by SEELE. His background, like Rei Ayanami's, is completely unknown. He has the amazing ability to change his synchronization rate at will, which astonished the NERV staff. He actively approached Shinji, and Shinji, too, opened his heart to Kaworu's straightforwardness and kindness. However, Kaworu was the seventeenth Angel, Tabris, sent in by SEELE, and he entered Terminal Dogma with the unmanned Unit-02 under his control. Then, of his own wish, he was crushed by Unit-01, in which Shinji rode. It is a well-known story that in the Japanese title of original episode 24, in which he appears, "The Final Messenger," joining the character for "shi" and the character for "sha" in the word "messenger" makes the surname of Kaworu: "Nagisa." See the entry "Kaworu Nagisa" in the character encyclopedia.
units.notes: Library entry 169; cross-series (Evangelion). The text is really about Kaworu Nagisa.
uncertain: The episode-24 wordplay is explained in prose; the Japanese characters cannot be shown in ASCII. Episode title rendered 'The Final Messenger' (official Netflix title).

units.en: The EVA series that SEELE, the secret organization that manages the Human Instrumentality Project, sent into NERV Headquarters to stop Gendo, who was advancing the plan outside its schedule. There are nine in total. Unlike the earlier series, the units' specifications include flight capability and S2 Engines as standard equipment. Dummy Plugs are used for activation and operation, and it seems that Kaworu Nagisa's data is in them.
units.notes: Library entry 170; cross-series (End of Evangelion).

units.en: The emperor of the Machine Empire Galfa, which plots the extermination of humanity. Originally the ecosystem management computer of the planet Alktos, the Emperor suddenly ran out of control, and tried to eliminate humanity, which destroys ecosystems, and become the king who manages the universe itself. The main body consists of seven programs and has a form resembling a seven-headed dragon. The Galfa Emperor and Zero function as mutual backup systems, and unless they are defeated at the same time they will revive. The Emperor is also protected by seven protections and can be defeated only by a simultaneous attack by seven Data Weapons.
units.notes: Library entry 171; cross-series (Dendoh).
uncertain: 'Alktos' per English Wikipedia ('Arcturus' is a possible alternate romanization of the kana).

units.en: A common soldier of the Machine Empire Galfa. By taking in other machines it evolves into a Galfa Machine Beast. A non-humanoid flying type (Type B) has also been confirmed.
units.notes: Library entry 172; cross-series (Dendoh). English Wikipedia name: 'Galfa Sotai'.

units.en: One of the Machine Professionals that infiltrated Earth hidden in meteorites; this one emerged from a meteorite that fell near Mikazuki Island. Machine Professionals are higher beings than Machine Beasts and possess advanced intelligence. It is good at high-speed aerial combat and can also transform into a flight form. The Photon Rifle is a versatile weapon that can also transform into a Photon Scythe.
units.notes: Library entry 173; cross-series (Dendoh).
uncertain: 'Machine Professional' for [jp] follows English Wikipedia ('Professional Machines').

units.en: One of the Machine Professionals that infiltrated Earth hidden in meteorites; this one emerged from a meteorite that fell in a wasteland on the Oceania continent. Its weapons are a photon laser fired from its forehead and electric shocks released from the wings on its back. It was the Machine Professional that dodged the Final Attack and remained to the end.
units.notes: Library entry 174; cross-series (Dendoh).
uncertain: Entries 173-175 and 181-182 are assigned to Virus/Error/Bug/Legacy/Lock by the unit-table offset; the English Wikipedia power lists do not match the library text exactly, so the Error/Bug assignment of 174/175 is the least certain.

units.en: One of the Machine Professionals that infiltrated Earth hidden in meteorites; this one emerged from a meteorite that fell in the Amazon jungle on the South American continent. It is good at tricky attacks with its freely extendable arms.
units.notes: Library entry 175; cross-series (Dendoh).

units.en: A Machine Beast born by taking in Earth's attack satellites. It was used in Galfa's first descent operation, and eighteen in total have been confirmed. As they gathered to respond to Dendoh's activation, they were all wiped out together by the Flash Lightning Blade Strike.
units.notes: Library entry 176; cross-series (Dendoh).
uncertain: 'Flash Lightning Blade Strike' ([jp]) translated literally; no English source.

units.en: A Machine Beast born by taking in a Defense Force fighter plane. Since it is based on a fighter plane, it has a variety of attacks such as missiles and machine guns.
units.notes: Library entry 177; cross-series (Dendoh).

units.name_jp: 機将ギガアブゾルート
units.en: One of the three officers of Spiral Castle. According to Ginga, "the third pompous guy." Its body is made of liquid metal, and it changes shape to dodge enemy attacks or entangle opponents. It also moves quickly and is good at surprise attacks, seeping into walls.
units.notes: Library entry 178; cross-series (Dendoh).
uncertain: Assignment of Absolute/Witter/Gourmet to 178/179/180 follows the unit-table order and matches the English Wikipedia power descriptions.

units.en: One of the three officers of Spiral Castle. According to Ginga, "a pompous kendama." It generates strong electromagnetic waves from its main body and has the ability to disable all electronic devices. Also, unless its head, the center, is destroyed, its body regenerates any number of times.
units.notes: Library entry 179; cross-series (Dendoh).
uncertain: 'Kendama' (cup-and-ball toy) kept as is.

units.en: One of the three officers of Spiral Castle. According to Ginga, "the pompous one, number two." It deploys an electromagnetic interference field around itself and has the ability to hinder the materialization of Data Weapons. It emits electric shocks from its arms and fires a beam cannon from its mouth. It is also quite a power fighter.
units.notes: Library entry 180; cross-series (Dendoh).

units.en: A Machine Professional that Subaru rides. Originally, like other Machine Professionals and Machine Beasts, it had thinking ability, but it has been modified so that a human can pilot it.
units.notes: Library entry 181; cross-series (Dendoh). The English spelling 'Legacy' is a guess from the kana (not on Wikipedia).

units.en: One of the Machine Professionals that infiltrated Earth hidden in meteorites; this one emerged from a meteorite that fell in the Sahara Desert on the African continent. It has the ability to make its whole body white-hot and explode everything around it.
units.notes: Library entry 182; cross-series (Dendoh).

units.en: A close aide of the Galfa Emperor, and the supreme officer of Galfa, who commands at the front lines in the Emperor's place. Excels at hand-to-hand combat and is good at staff fighting with an extendable ruyi staff. Also has the fearsome special ability to revive immediately even if destroyed. Often travels, or makes combined attacks, riding on the back of the heavy machine beast Vector, which has interstellar navigation ability.
units.notes: Library entry 183; cross-series (Dendoh).

units.en: Zero's strongest form, combined with the heavy machine beast Vector. Armed with a huge lancer and photon blasters fired from both shoulders, it is greatly powered up in both combat power and mobility. Incidentally, heavy machine beast is the general term for Machine Beasts that were promoted because they achieved results when Galfa invaded other planets before attacking Earth, and having gained that much experience, they are individuals stronger than ordinary Machine Beasts.
units.notes: Library entry 184; cross-series (Dendoh).

units.en: A black Gear that forms a pair with Dendoh. It is also called Knight Ouga. Its basic abilities are the same as Dendoh's, but it has been modified to be single-seat. It is piloted by Arthea, captain of the Galfa Emperor's guard, and like Dendoh it has the ability to file-save Data Weapons.
units.notes: Library entry 185; cross-series (Dendoh). English Wikipedia: 'Knight Gear Oger'.
uncertain: 'Ouga' vs. Wikipedia 'Oger/Ogre'.

units.name_jp: 凰牙・バイパーウィップ
units.en: An Ouga fitted with Viper Whip. Viper Whip seeks "confidence," so Arthea became its owner.
units.notes: Library entry 186; cross-series (Dendoh).

units.en: An Ouga fitted with Bull Horn. The "wisdom" that Bull Horn seeks was also greater in Arthea.
units.notes: Library entry 187; cross-series (Dendoh).

units.en: A Machine Beast adjusted for capturing Data Weapons. Because of that purpose its combat ability is low, and it carries out operations in combination with other Machine Beasts.
units.notes: Library entry 188; cross-series (Dendoh).

units.en: The Galfa Emperor's pet. It is not a mechanical life form, but a space creature that eats machines. For that reason, it is sometimes used to punish subordinates who failed. The Lagou virus, a computer virus that is a deadly poison to machines, is implanted in the fangs hidden in Lagou's huge jaws.
units.notes: Library entry 189; cross-series (Dendoh).

units.en: The master of Spiral Castle, sent to conquer Earth, called "Oyakata-sama" (the Lord). Three Machine Generals serve under it, and it is the apex of the pyramid that includes the Machine Beasts below them. A Spiral Castle is a unit of the Galfa army, and countless Spiral Castles exist throughout the universe.
units.notes: Library entry 190; cross-series (Dendoh).
uncertain: 'Oyakata-sama' kept in romanization with a gloss.

units.en: A super-large battleship of the Jovian Federation. Over ten times the size of the Nadesico, it is closer to a fortress than a battleship. In the Lizard War, Commander-in-Chief Haruki Kusakabe boarded it, and it was operated as the flagship of the Yujin Corps of the Jovian Federation Forces.
units.notes: Library entry 191; cross-series (Nadesico).
uncertain: 'Yujin Corps' and 'Jovian Federation Forces' translated from the kana wording.

units.en: An unmanned combat weapon of the Jovian Federation. It is classified as an insect-type fighter in the Jovian Federation, but on Earth it is mainly called by the name of the creature whose shape it resembles. These unmanned combat weapons are produced at the phase transition engine plants discovered in the Jupiter region, and since they are products of an ancient civilization, overtechnology such as small anti-gravity propulsion devices is used.
units.notes: Library entry 192; cross-series (Nadesico).

units.en: An unmanned combat weapon of the Jovian Federation. Joro is a spider-type robot named for its resemblance to the Joro spider. The abdominal unit can be swapped for self-destruct explosives and other loads depending on the mission.
units.notes: Library entry 193; cross-series (Nadesico).

units.en: An unmanned combat weapon of the Jovian Federation. It is an upper-grade model of Batta, the most popular unmanned combat weapon. A field generator is attached, giving it excellent defense. Compared with Batta, machine guns have been removed in terms of armament, but it makes up for this with ramming attacks that take advantage of its high defense.
units.notes: Library entry 194; cross-series (Nadesico).

units.en: A manned humanoid combat weapon of the Jovian Federation. It is a weapon-reinforced version of Tetsujin, which was modeled on Gekiganger from Gekiganger 3, the sacred text of the Jovian Federation. The Jin series can make solo boson jumps without going through a Tulip, but the jump distance is limited to short range. Even so, that was sufficient for the purpose of breaking through the enemy front line and delivering a powerful blow to the core.
units.notes: Library entry 195; cross-series (Nadesico).

units.en: A manned humanoid combat weapon of the Jovian Federation. It is a weapon-reinforced version of Majin, which was modeled on Umiganger from Gekiganger 3, the sacred text of the Jovian Federation. Because the Jin series carry phase transition reactors, they are large machines exceeding 30 m, and the Dai class, the weapon-reinforced version, is larger still.
units.notes: Library entry 196; cross-series (Nadesico).
uncertain: 'Umiganger' and 'Rikuganger' are romanized from kana (no English source).

units.en: A manned humanoid combat weapon of the Jovian Federation. It is a machine modeled on Rikuganger from Gekiganger 3, the sacred text of the Jovian Federation. A late-model Jin, it was shaped with anti-field combat in mind so that close-combat ability does not decline after the Gekigan Punch is fired. Naturally, a weapon-reinforced Daidenjin was also planned, but the war ended before roll-out.
units.notes: Library entry 197; cross-series (Nadesico).

units.en: An unmanned destroyer of the Jovian Federation. Like other unmanned machines, it is also produced at the plants. Because it is mass-produced, it has the simplest block structure among the Jovian Federation's warships, and several variations can be made just by swapping the combat block and the power block.
units.notes: Library entry 198; cross-series (Nadesico).

units.en: A mobile weapon of the Martian Successors. Pronounced "Shishiki." Miniaturization was achieved by making the boson jump system an external unit. The Martian Successors' machines are developed, based on Kusakabe's philosophy, on the premise of assault tactics using boson jumps. Shishiki's boson jump is limited to a single use, and it excels at surprise attack and charge tactics that take advantage of that ability.
units.notes: Library entry 199; cross-series (Nadesico movie).

units.en: A machine of Hokushin's Six. Pronounced "Mutsura." An airframe that omits the legs and emphasizes mobility, and it is also capable of a single-use boson jump through an external unit. It excels at "Kugutsu-mai" (Puppet Dance), an irregular mobile attack that uses rotating turret nozzles. Like Yatenko, it also has a field generator around the cockpit.
units.notes: Library entry 200; cross-series (Nadesico movie). The batch label was Iron Sand.
uncertain: 'Hokushin's Six' is a translation of [jp] (no English source).

units.en: A mobile weapon that Hokushin rides. Pronounced "Yatenko." It is a compact developed version of the Jin series that the Jovian Federation operated during the Lizard War, and although there is a limit on the number of times, it can make multiple mid-range boson jumps. Since it can move to the battlefield by boson jump, it uses fuel-type thrusters and excels at the irregular movement called "Kugutsu-mai" (Puppet Dance). It is also equipped with three small distortion field generators around the cockpit, making it a machine with high survivability.
units.notes: Library entry 201; cross-series (Nadesico movie). The batch label was Asura.

units.en: The prototype of a giant Metal Armor developed at the Giganos secret weapons factory. A walking ammunition depot with a 12-barrel chest machine cannon, a 100-tube missile pod, a quad Vulcan cannon, large cruise missiles and more built in. It carries a control system that allows operation by thought, enabling high mobility far beyond normal reaction speed. However, this system was unfinished and placed a heavy burden on the pilot, so it could not be used for long periods. In addition, the installed sensors had a serious flaw: they could not distinguish overlapping targets.
units.notes: Library entry 202; batch label was Gades. Unit-table name Gilgazamune.

units.en: Dorchenov's personal Gilgazamune. It is equipped with a long sword instead of an Azure Dragon sword. Unfortunately, the sensor flaw has not been fixed.
units.notes: Library entry 203; batch label was Casmodon. Variant of Gilgazamune.

units.en: A mass-production Gilgazamune. The huge close-combat HB saber fitted at the request of Colonel Gon Jem seems to have been officially adopted.
units.notes: Library entry 204; batch label was Grujios. Variant of Gilgazamune.

units.en: A prototype Metal Armor of the Giganos forces. A high-performance machine that Gon Jem used as his personal unit, but it seems it never reached mass production. The grenades at the waist and the Azure Dragon sword on the back seem to reflect Gon Jem's tastes. Its attack power was nonetheless high, and the Azure Dragon sword, coated with a special alloy, combined with Gon Jem's skill, was sharp enough to cut through even the D-1's shield. The cobra painted on the shoulder is the emblem of the Gon Jem Squad.
units.notes: Library entry 205; batch label was Zarios. Unit-table name Geizam ([jp]).

units.en: A machine made by fitting a Maffu flight unit to the Gewei, the main mass-production Metal Armor of the Giganos forces. Its weapons are a 50 mm hand rail gun and a 30 mm machine cannon built into the camera-eye section. Because development of the Maffu unit was rushed, its flight ability is somewhat inferior to the others.
units.notes: Library entry 206; batch label was Diondra.

units.en: A machine made by fitting a Maffu flight unit to the Gelf, a high-performance Metal Armor deployed only in small numbers to the Practice Squad and the Imperial Guard Armored Division. The Gelfs that the Practice Squad ride are painted in special colors. It can be called a simplified Falguen, and has Simole Type-A passive armor and a radar more sensitive than a maiden's skin.
units.notes: Library entry 207; batch label was Devil Saturn 6.
uncertain: 'Imperial Guard Armored Division' vs. 'Armored Corps' used elsewhere (the library writes both [jp]/[jp]).

units.en: A bike-type Metal Armor. It can split into upper and lower parts and recombine, with the upper turret part called Dolla and the lower bike part called Ganzer. Dolla can transform into a semi-humanoid form and fly, and by swapping the lower part for Gelfer, it becomes Geldolla, a marine Metal Armor. It is used for parachute drop operations and the like.
units.notes: Library entry 208; batch label was Falgos. Unit-table name Stark Gandolla.
uncertain: 'Ganzer', 'Gelfer', 'Geldolla' are romanized from kana (no English source).

units.en: A Gewei customized exclusively for Captain Gol. It has not only been reinforced with a 450 mm rail cannon and hand grenades, but its output has also been greatly increased, making it a machine worthy of the brawny Captain Gol. The cockpit modifications must have been a lot of work.
units.notes: Library entry 209; batch label was Phenomena. Unit-table name Stark Gewei.
uncertain: The last sentence is the author's own conjecture in the Japanese; kept as a comment.

units.en: The giant battleship that King Vega boards. It was used when escaping the explosion of planet Vega, and flew to the Skull Moon base using the space transposition device Transportion. It fires powerful beams from the protrusions at the front of the hull, and can produce smoke to hide itself and a powerful barrier from the many holes on the side of the hull. In the end it is destroyed by the concentrated attack of the Grendizer team.
units.notes: Library entry 246; batch label was Gilgazamune. Cross-series (Grendizer).
uncertain: 'Transportion' is romanized from kana.

units.en: The first Vega Beast, stronger than the Saucer Beasts. Vega Beasts are wild animals turned into cyborgs, and have greater combat power than Saucer Beasts. In addition to power strong enough to tear off Grendizer's left arm, it has an excellent sense of smell, and can remember the scent of an opponent it has fought once and hunt that opponent down no matter where. Because its origin is a gorilla, it has a tendency to be afraid of fire. Also, as is the convention for an enlarged gorilla, it took Hikaru hostage and climbed to the top of a skyscraper and roared. It is the Vega Beast with the most memorable name.
units.notes: Library entry 247; batch label was Gilgazamune. Cross-series (Grendizer).

units.en: The strongest and last Vega Beast, which Lady Gandal boarded. A large amount of Vegatron energy was injected into it, and it has tremendous power and a sturdy body. It breathes high-temperature flames from its mouth, and the beams fired from the two protrusions on its chest not only damage the machine but also temporarily take away the opponent's sight.
units.notes: Library entry 248; batch label was Gilgazamune. Cross-series (Grendizer).

units.en: A Vega Beast piloted by Imperial Guard captain Morus. It originally had flesh, but on the last day of planet Vega, because Vega exploded when the transfer machine was activated, it was transferred by mistake to the very edge of the solar system, and on its way to Skull Moon it was reduced to bones by meteorites and cosmic rays. It fires powerful beams from its eyes and pierces enemies with the drill in its chest.
units.notes: Library entry 249; batch label was Geizam. Cross-series (Grendizer).

units.en: A Vega Beast equipped with a freezing ray, developed by the genius girl Kirika. It fires the freezing ray from its pupils and from the gem on its chest, and together with the blade on its right hand it gave Grendizer a hard time. The freezing ray was originally meant to cool the temperature of young planets, but was converted into a weapon by King Vega's order.
units.notes: Library entry 250; batch label was Gewei Maffu. Cross-series (Grendizer).

units.en: A giant saucer battleship that launches from the Skull Moon base on the Moon. Normally it is hung from the symbol tower of Skull Moon. Under the command of Captain Blacky, it served as a combat mothership carrying Saucer Beasts and Mini Fours. It has powerful beam cannons and sturdy armor.
units.notes: Library entry 251; batch label was Gelf Maffu. Cross-series (Grendizer).
uncertain: 'Mother Barn' vs. 'Mother Burn' (kana [jp]).

units.en: A medium-sized space saucer of the Vega Star Union Forces. It is about twice the size of the Mini Four, and its weapons are a Vegatron beam cannon and two missiles. Like the Mini Four, it excels at group combat, but it was not much of a threat to Grendizer.
units.notes: Library entry 252; batch label was Stark Gandolla. Cross-series (Grendizer).
uncertain: 'Vega Star Union Forces' translated from the kana wording.

units.en: A small space saucer of the Vega Star Union Forces. They appear in groups and attack in formation. Their weapons are Vegatron beam cannons and missiles. Besides combat, they are also used for reconnaissance and transport. They were a sufficient threat to the TFO, but because they were weak against Grendizer, most were destroyed in one hit. There are two kinds, for attack and for work, which differ in color.
units.notes: Library entry 253; batch label was Stark Gewei. Cross-series (Grendizer).

units.en: A Saucer Beast that sortied to support the Great Mazinger operated by Barendos. It attacks with disc-shaped arms with protrusions on the outside and three sharp legs. It is destroyed by the Atomic Punch of the Great Mazinger that Koji boarded.
units.notes: Library entry 254; batch label was Stark Deins. Cross-series (Grendizer vs. Great Mazinger).

units.en: A Saucer Beast that was inside the spherical giant beam cannon of the Barendos battleship. It is made of charged energy in the air, so no solid-projectile weapons work on it at all. It is broken apart by the Anti-Gravity Storm and Breast Burn, but it rammed Grendizer with the three spheres inside its body. Although it calls itself a Saucer Beast, it cannot transform into a saucer.
units.notes: Library entry 255; batch label was Stark Dautzen. Cross-series (Grendizer vs. Great Mazinger).

units.en: A Saucer Beast that Barendos deployed to capture the TFO. It extends its hook-claw-shaped hands to catch its opponent. It strangles Grendizer, which is fighting the Great Mazinger, from behind, but is destroyed by the Anti-Gravity Storm.
units.notes: Library entry 256; batch label was Deins Maffu. Cross-series (Grendizer vs. Great Mazinger).

units.en: A space monster that can be called both mechanical and biological, released into Japan by aliens plotting to conquer the Earth. It has a hard outer shell, a lizard-like face and an insect-type body, and spits out a dissolving liquid from its mouth. It grows by eating iron, and it ate the arm of the Great Mazinger.
units.notes: Library entry 257; batch label was Dreu. Cross-series (Mazinger movies).

units.en: Gilgilgan's second form. It has the appearance of a humanoid upper body growing out of the back of the first form. It has become able to shoot rays from the lizard eyes of the lower body.
units.notes: Library entry 258; batch label was Dragonar-1 Custom. Cross-series (Mazinger movies).

units.en: Gilgilgan's final form. It ate the aliens' saucer filled with cosmic energy, grew huge and became humanoid. It has wings and can fly. Its weapons are a sickle-like weapon on its waist and rays from its fingertips. It shows overwhelming strength, but its weak point is figured out to be the base of the sickle, and it is destroyed by a joint operation of the Great Mazinger and Getter Robo.
units.notes: Library entry 259; batch label was Falguen Maffu. Cross-series (Mazinger movies).

units.en: A weapon that looks like a space creature, released by mysterious aliens plotting to invade the Earth. It entangled Getter Robo with the tentacles growing all over its body and tried to slam it into the ground. It also fires strange rays from its eyes. It exploded from the suicide charge of Bear Go. It drove Musashi to his death.
units.notes: Library entry 260; batch label was Yakt Gelf Maffu. Cross-series (Mazinger movies).
uncertain: Name 'Gurangen' romanized from the kana; unverified.
'Musashi' = Musashi Tomoe (male) per Wikipedia; 'his death' follows from that.

units.en: A combat weapon of mysterious aliens. It is an assembly of fighter planes, tanks, the main guns of battleships and the like, and can fire from all over its body. It has the special ability to return to its original form again, if the individual parts are undamaged, even after being broken into pieces.
units.notes: Library entry 261; batch label was Levi Gelf Maffu. Cross-series (Mazinger movies).
uncertain: Name 'Bong' romanized from the kana; unverified.

units.en: The final combat weapon of mysterious aliens. Light wraps its whole body, and it absorbs beam and other light-ray energy and grows huge. Solid-projectile weapons, too, are deflected by the light. In addition to firing arrows of light that destroy the opponent from the inside, it has sharp claws and missiles from its chest. After the light was stripped away by the Great Typhoon and its mechanical body was exposed, it was destroyed by the Great Booster.
units.notes: Library entry 262; batch label was Dolla. Cross-series (Mazinger movies).
uncertain: Name 'Pikudoron' romanized from the kana; unverified.

units.en: A creature that had been lurking in the sea in ancient times, which revived and grew huge because humans spilled oil into the sea. For that reason it loves oil and attacks tankers. It can fly, and the dragon's-neck-shaped tentacles regenerate instantly even if cut, and can also be rotated to create strong winds. Also, its flexible body is immune to missile attacks.
units.notes: Library entry 263; batch label was Dautzen. Cross-series (Mazinger movies).

pilots.en: A powerful commander who once even took the No. 1 spot in the Gyandlar Commander ranking, in place of Devil Saturn 6. Asura fires Nattoru bullets, which rob the target of bodily freedom, from the abdomen, and specializes in destroying the immobilized opponent in cruel ways. By nature Asura is cruel and cunning, and once set a trap by turning Rom's party's surprise attack plan against them. Asura drove Baikanfu into a corner, but was pierced through the chest by Thunder Cyclone and defeated.
pilots.notes: Text identical to unit entry 157; translation reused.
uncertain: Gender of Asura unknown: no pronouns used.
'Nattoru bullet' is romanized from kana (no English source).

pilots.en: The boss of the space crime organization Gyandlar. Gyandlar's goal is to rule the entire universe and bring darkness and fear. It is also searching for Hyribead, an infinite energy said to grant eternal life. Gadess is a villain who has wandered space for thousands of years piling up evil deeds, and trusts no one but himself. His sorcerous power is such that he can paralyze enemies in distant places. He attacked planet Cronos after Hyribead, but his ambition was thwarted by the Cronos tribe warriors, including Rom. He hates having rust form on his body to an extreme degree, and always kept with him a dedicated robot, Bibibi Mouse, to polish his body.
pilots.notes: Text identical to unit entry 158; translation reused.
uncertain: Gender male per ja Wikipedia/voice actors (glossary).
'Bibibi Mouse' romanized from kana.

pilots.en: The true form of Gyandlar executive Garudi. In truth, he is Rom and Leina's real older brother, whom they had thought dead since early childhood. He was picked up by Gadess, who valued his talent for Tenku Shin Ken, and for a long time he underwent mind control as a Gyandlar executive. (The fearsome appearance of Garudi is also thought to be part of that control.) In the final episode of the original story, he gives his own sword to his beloved younger brother Rom and orders him to cut down Gadess.
uncertain: 'Garudi' vs. 'Guardi' (English Wikipedia uses both).
The parenthetical refers to Garudi's armored/fearsome look; 'fearsome appearance of Garudi' is my rendering of 'ikatsui Garudi no sugata'.

pilots.en: A low-ranking Gyandlar Commander. When first introduced, Casmodon appeared as the main enemy and tried to set the Cronos tribe and the Battle tribe against each other, but after that appeared in large numbers as a grunt. Casmodon can transform into a flight form like a jet aircraft.
pilots.notes: Text identical to unit entry 159; translation reused.
uncertain: Gender unknown: 'Casmodon' repeated.

pilots.en: One of the Gyandlar executives. Fond of underhanded schemes and plots, Grujios serves as a kind of strategist for Gyandlar. With tremendous sorcerous power, Grujios can revive the ghosts of Gyandlar Commanders and use them as servants. In truth, the real body is only a caterpillar-like face floating in the tank of the head. Grujios was defeated by Rom in the Battle of the Heavenly Demon Castle, but, just as promised in the "I shall return" warning, came back in spirit form. After becoming a spirit, Grujios gained a new ability to take over other people's bodies, and tormented Rom's party by posing as an ally.
pilots.notes: Text identical to unit entry 160; translation reused.
uncertain: Gender unknown: no pronouns used.
'Battle of the Heavenly Demon Castle' is my translation of the event name.

pilots.en: A low-ranking Gyandlar Commander. Zarios is characterized by caterpillar-track legs, but had no especially notable role in the original story.
pilots.notes: Text identical to unit entry 161; translation reused.

pilots.en: A female Gyandlar executive. In contrast to Grujios, so to speak, she often takes direct command at the front lines. Devil Saturn 6 are her direct subordinates. Wielding an electromagnetic whip, her speech and attitude fit being called "Big Sis," but she gets angry when called that. She is bold and cruel by nature, and tries to compete with Grujios at every turn. She also has a cute side in that she is actually afraid of earthquakes, and in the original story she almost got on good terms with Tough Trailer for a moment. After that, she set a trap for Tough Trailer by making that character hold the Medusa demon sword, a cursed blade that drives its holder mad, but after that scheme failed, she herself came to favor the Medusa demon sword. She can also breathe fire from her mouth and emit hypnotic light from her eyes.
pilots.notes: Text identical to unit entry 162; translation reused.
uncertain: Tough Trailer's gender is not sourced, so no pronoun is used for that character.
'Big Sis' for the nickname Aneego (boss-lady / older-sister).

pilots.en: The combined form of Devil Saturn No. 1 through No. 6. Thanks to its viciousness and power it has held the No. 1 spot in the Gyandlar Commander ranking; it dropped in rank once, but soon came back. Its attacks are varied: not only fighting, but also flames from the mouth, claws launched on chains, beams from the eyes, and so on. It once even devised the Devil Foot Smash to counter God Hand Smash. It was often entrusted with Gyandlar's field operations, and was beaten up by Rom and the others time after time. It is a commander whose odd Kansai dialect makes it hard to hate, but in fact only Devil Saturn No. 1 actually uses the Kansai dialect, and the other five speak standard Japanese.
pilots.notes: Text identical to unit entry 163; translation reused.
uncertain: 'Devil Saturn' vs. English Wikipedia 'Devil Satan'.
'God Hand Smash' is a translation of the kana (Rom/Baikanfu technique).

pilots.en: Leina's servant, who can transform into three forms: robot, jet helicopter and supercar. Technically a member of the Jet tribe. Because Triple Jim can carry members of the Cronos tribe, Jim is a great help when traveling, but is poor at fighting because of a gentle nature. That said, Jim understands how martial artists feel, and often put Jim's own body on the line for Leina's sake. Always humble and polite in speech, Jim shouts "It is above you, if you please!" even when warning someone that something is falling from above. In episode 24, Jim performed a catchphrase imitating Rom's. Jim also seems to be able to use Tenku Chushin Ken, though only a little.
pilots.notes: Text identical to unit entry 1; translation reused.
uncertain: Gender unknown: 'Jim' repeated instead of a pronoun.
The line shouted ('above, if you please') is a paraphrase of the polite 'ue de gozaimasu'.

pilots.en: The former top disciple of Rom's father, Kirai Stol. A member of the Cronos tribe who is an elder disciple to Rom and the others. He learned Tenku Chushin Ken and surpassed his master in offensive techniques, but Kirai saw through his character, which sought only power, and did not permit him full mastery. Resenting this, he ran away from Kirai, and was living as a bandit when Gyandlar invited him, though Diondra seems to have thought he would be thrown away once he had served his purpose. He wields the forbidden technique "Tenku Chushin Ken: Electromagnetic Poison Hand-Blade." The poison hand-blade is a hand-blade into which poison has been soaked by dipping the hand in all kinds of deadly poisons; even a graze lets poison into the body through the wound and kills the opponent. He is also good at finger bullets, and has a technique called "Tenku Chushin Ken: Dark Finger Bullet."
uncertain: 'Elder disciple' for the kana wording (anideshi).
Technique names translated from the Japanese (no English source).

pilots.en: A low-ranking Gyandlar Commander. Its agility is its trait, but it seems not to have been depicted much in the original story.
pilots.notes: Text identical to unit entry 164; translation reused.

pilots.en: A warrior of the Jet tribe who, like Rom and Drill, trained under Kirai. He was taught Tenku Shin Ken by Kirai. As his name suggests, he can transform into a jet aircraft. Within Rom's party he is the cool, handsome type, who dashes in to rescue friends and beautiful women in their moment of crisis. He is also quite sharp, and often served as Rom's strategist. His only built-in weapon is the sword stored at his waist, from which he unleashes various secret techniques of Tenku Shin Ken. The Blazer Cannon is an additional weapon that appeared from the middle of the original story; it has the same name as Rod Drill's, but the cannon on Jet fires beams.
pilots.notes: Text identical to unit entry 6; translation reused.

pilots.en: Rom's younger sister. She goes along on Rom's journey, accompanied by Triple Jim. Although not to the degree her brother is, she has some knowledge of Tenku Chushin Ken, and has shown the Mantis Fist, the Rock-Breaking Fist and the Gale Kick. She is cheerful and active by nature, and somewhat overly devoted to her brother. For that reason, she often frets over her brother, who is popular wherever they travel. She loves fortune-telling, but no matter how many times she does it, it seems to say she is fated never to meet a wonderful person. At first she was treated like a princess, but later she rides the Power Riser and takes an active part in battle. In episode 37 she delivered a somewhat awkward catchphrase, but the catchphrase she delivered when she became the lead in a later video series was truly polished.
uncertain: 'Rock-Breaking Fist' and 'Gale Kick' are my translations of the technique names.

pilots.en: A fellow disciple of Rom and Jet. He is from the Battle tribe and transforms into a drill tank. Cheerful and bold, he excels at power-based fighting. He was something of a mood maker within the party, yet repeatedly saved his companions from danger with that drill. He is the type who sleeps a full 10 hours, and apparently once punched Jet in his sleep when Jet came to wake him. He has no built-in weapons, and since his trademark drill cannot be used in this form either, he fights with his fists alone, but he rarely shouts technique names; the only one confirmed is "Tenku Chushin Ken: Head-Hunting." The Blazer Cannon differs from Jet's in the shape of its muzzle, and is a missile launcher.
pilots.notes: Text identical to unit entry 8; translation reused.
uncertain: 'Tenku Chushin Ken: Head-Hunting' is my translation of the technique name (no English source).
'Fellow disciple' for the kana 'brother disciple'.

pilots.en: A Cronos tribe warrior and martial artist living on planet Cronos. The son of Kirai, the Taoist master who founded Tenku Chushin Ken, he has attained full mastery of both Tenku Chushin Ken and Tenku Shin Ken. Rom likes to use "Tenku Chushin Ken: Whirlwind Kick." The purpose of Tenku Chushin Ken is to defeat evil and protect justice and truth, and in fact Rom's family are aliens who came to planet Cronos to build up their strength. He values justice above all and has a strong heart that never forgives evil, but he seems to be bad with women. Also, although he is polite and strict with himself, he seems to be a little soft on his younger sister Leina. By drawing out the power of Kenro, the sword inherited from his father, he can merge into the giant robots Kenryu and Baikanfu. With his many Tenku Chushin Ken techniques and a distinctive catchphrase that he delivers suddenly, from out of nowhere, he plunges villains into the depths of terror, and after defeating Gyandlar, he sets off across dimensions (reincarnates) to save a universe ruled by darkness. Incidentally, in the original story Kenryu and Baikanfu are petrified and left behind on planet Cronos at that time.
uncertain: 'Taoist master' for [jp].
'Whirlwind Kick' is my translation of the technique name.

pilots.en: Kaine's mother. She is divorced from her husband, Jim Austin, who was an Alliance soldier. She worked at the immigration control center of the colony Alucard, but went missing during the fighting with Giganos. A woman faithful to her duties and valuing ethics, she is someone Kaine respects, though he does not say so out loud.

pilots.name_jp: ウェルナー・フリッツ
pilots.en: A member of the Practice Squad, the elite unit under Meio. He is 19 years old and holds the rank of warrant officer. Even among the three, his eyes are especially nasty. The Practice Squad's loyalty to Meio is strong, reaching the level of worship.
uncertain: 'Practice Squad' follows English Wikipedia; the kana is Practices ([jp]).
Gender: male, from the 'boys' unit' wording elsewhere and the group description.

pilots.en: A member of the Practice Squad, the elite unit under Meio. He is 19 years old and holds the rank of warrant officer. When first introduced, the Practice Squad was an obnoxious elite group, but as the story progressed, their devoted actions toward Meio won support, and they gained fans.

One of Gon Jem's Four Heavenly Kings, who pilots the Stark Gandolla. His rank is captain. Fittingly for the Gon Jem Squad, which is called "Giganos's filth," he has an extremely cruel personality, and is described as a murderer wearing a military uniform. He has a big scar on his face and always has a 5-sun (about 15 cm) nail in his mouth. Maybe he is short on iron.
uncertain: '5-sun nail' kept with the metric gloss.
'Giganos's filth' ([jp]) vs. English Wikipedia 'Garbage of Giganos'.

pilots.en: The founder and supreme ruler of the United Empire Giganos. It seems he was originally a high-ranking officer of some country. He starts the invasion of Earth to eliminate everyone and every idea belonging to the Earth Alliance as inferior and create a new order in space. He loves Earth so much that, in order to wipe out the Alliance forces without harming Earth's beauty, he even carries out pinpoint attacks using mass drivers. He holds an elitist ideology of thoroughgoing ability supremacy, and keeps as pets rumble fish, which kill each other if several are put in the same tank.
uncertain: 'Rumble fish' translated from the kana ([jp]).

pilots.en: The commander of the Asia theater secret guard unit of Giganos. His rank is colonel. He has four skilled subordinates called Gon Jem's Four Heavenly Kings. He is rough and vulgar by nature, and that shows in his way of fighting too: even in Metal Armor combat, he excels at close combat with a huge Azure Dragon sword. Having done a number of dirty jobs, he seems to have connections in the military. He is also surprisingly caring toward his subordinates and is trusted by them. With a sacred straw rope (shimenawa) strung around his neck, he resembles a Tosa fighting dog.
uncertain: 'Gon Jem' (English Wikipedia) vs. kana 'Gun Jem'.
'Shimenawa' kept and glossed.

pilots.en: A 16-year-old civilian boy who lived on the space colony Alucard and attends the Astronaut Academy. His parents are divorced; his father is a staff officer of the Alliance forces and his mother works at the colony's immigration control center. He gets along well with Tapp and Light. During Giganos's attack on Alucard, the three happened to be on the scene in town where a man carrying a data disk of a secret weapon was shot dead by someone, and were entrusted with the disk by the man as he died, and they ended up becoming pilots of the secret weapon, the Dragonars. However, since the Dragonars had a system that could be piloted only by those who had completed pilot registration, they went along with the Alliance forces as events unfolded. By personality he is more of a flirt, but he is a straightforward type who acts without thinking too much, and the typical bully-boy type, oddly loyal and with a strong sense of justice. As a result he stirs up trouble here and there and drags those around him in. His hairstyle was originally a pompadour, but the demon sergeant cut it, giving him his current look. He falls in love at first sight with Linda, whom he met as a refugee from the Moon.
uncertain: 'Kaine' (Wikipedia/MAL) vs. fan spelling 'Kane'.
'Bully-boy type' translates the idiom 'gaki daisho' (kid ringleader).

pilots.en: One of Gon Jem's Four Heavenly Kings, who pilots the Stark Gewei. His rank is captain. He is the biggest man in the Gon Jem Squad, with a skeleton that does not seem human, but his wits are weak to match. He has a very violent personality and a habit of firing his machine cannon everywhere when something displeases him, which is extremely annoying. Looking for a wife.

pilots.name_jp: ジェームス・Ｃ・ダグラス
pilots.en: A soldier of the Earth Alliance Forces, with the rank of lieutenant. The official pilot of Dragonar-1. Because Kaine stole the Dragonar-1 that he should rightfully have ridden, he reluctantly became the training officer for Kaine and the others, an unfortunate man. Perhaps for that reason, although he is a capable soldier, he got no further than captain even after promotions. He becomes a crying drunk when he gets drunk.
uncertain: Gender from the game text ('kare') and ja Wikipedia.
'Training officer' for [jp].

pilots.en: One of Gon Jem's Four Heavenly Kings, who pilots the Stark Dautzen. His rank is lieutenant. He has looks that could be called handsome, but among the four he is the most calculating, cold-blooded and vindictive. His manner of death was, truly, too awful. I cannot forget the sight of him threatening Linda while licking a knife.
uncertain: The last sentence is the writer's own first-person comment in the Japanese ('forgettable') and is kept as such.

pilots.en: One of the refugees aboard the transport ship Idaho, a mysterious beautiful teacher. In truth, however, she is a second lieutenant of Earth Alliance Forces intelligence, in charge of monitoring the D-Weapons and guarding Linda. At 22, she is the most adult of the three heroines. She is a big-sister figure to Linda and Rose, and is calm and composed. Perhaps for that reason she gets along with Light, but it did not progress much. A mature woman full of kindness and consideration for others, she has the flaw of being a bad drunk.
uncertain: 'Second lieutenant' for [jp] (English Wikipedia says only 'Lt').

pilots.en: A 16-year-old student at the same Astronaut Academy as Kaine, from New York. He becomes the pilot of Dragonar-2. He is the so-called "gentle and strong" type, but like Kaine and the others, a cheerful boy with a light attitude. He is family-minded, and sends part of his military pay to his parents and younger sister living in New York. Influenced by his parents, who were musicians, he loves music, and his treasured CD player is, by his own account, the third most important thing to him after his life. He particularly likes rock and jazz. His dream for the future is to work in show business and run a theater that stages musicals and the like. A self-declared and generally acknowledged "feminist" (in the Japanese sense of being gallant toward women), he gets on good terms with Rose before anyone notices.
uncertain: 'Feminist' in the Japanese sense of a man who is gallant toward women; kept in quotes with a gloss.
'Gentle and strong' translates the set phrase 'ki wa yasashikute chikara mochi'.

pilots.en: A member of the Practice Squad, the elite unit under Meio. He is 19 years old and holds the rank of warrant officer. The Practice Squad was also called the "boys' unit," which is an apt description. He is the only one of the three to die in battle, and that, too, was to protect Meio, as one would expect.

A lieutenant colonel of the Giganos Empire. Known as a radical, he proposes indiscriminate all-out attacks with mass drivers, and so on. Each time, however, Guiltorre admonishes him, and he seems to be inwardly irritated that his opinions are not accepted. He is interested only in winning this war and has no perspective on what to do with the world after the war. He is an ambitious man with both baseness and pettiness, but the image of a small-fry sticks to him.
uncertain: 'Dorchenov' (Wikipedia) vs. 'Dolchenov'.

pilots.en: His full name is Lang Plato. He is the father of Linda and Meio. A scientist who was the chief of Metal Armor development for the Giganos military and who designed and developed the three Dragonars. But to weed out the seeds of war he had sown himself, after the outbreak of war he defected to the Earth Alliance with the Dragonars, and is working on the Dragoon mass-production plan at the Chongqing base. His love for his family is deep, as shown by his remembering the clothing size of his ex-wife, but it does not seem to get through to his children very well. Despite carrying a heavy past, he normally plays a cheerful old guy. His favorite food is Chinese steamed buns.

The demon sergeant appointed as the training officer for Kaine and the others. It is hard enough just to give soldier training to the three goofballs, and as the person in charge of training he is also scolded by Lieutenant Douglas, so it is a thankless role. In the end, however, considering that he marries a certain person, he can be called a lucky man. He has a bold personality, but is surprisingly meticulous, and is a dependable big-brother figure to the three.
uncertain: Gender: no English source states it; male assumed from ja Wikipedia (he marries Diane) and the 'big brother' wording. Flag if a source says otherwise.

pilots.en: A young ace of the Giganos Imperial Guard Armored Corps, known as the "Blue Hawk of Giganos." He is 24 years old with the rank of captain. He agrees with the ideology of Giganos and is trusted by Guiltorre, but carries the burden of being the son of a traitor. Calm and confident, he is blessed with the qualities of a commander who makes accurate decisions, and he has many believers within the military. For that reason he also has many enemies, and attempts to bring him down never cease. In the latter half of the story he completely steals the show with his activity, and is highly regarded as the hidden protagonist. The last scene of the final episode in particular is a must-see.
uncertain: 'Meio' (Wikipedia/MAL) vs. kana Maillo/Maillot.

pilots.en: One of Gon Jem's Four Heavenly Kings, a tall woman who pilots the Stark Deins. Her rank is captain. She is quite strong, and it is said that no one who teased her got away unharmed. She is the sole woman in the Gon Jem Squad and a gutsy big-sister figure, but shows a cute side toward a man she acknowledges as stronger than herself. Her skill is solid, and she survived to the end even after the Gon Jem Squad was wiped out, and snatched the best parts.

A 17-year-old student at the same Astronaut Academy as Kaine, who carries noble blood. He becomes the pilot of Dragonar-3. He is deeply versed in electronics, and seems to have taken to Dragonar-3, the electronic warfare machine, at first sight. Among the three he is comparatively calm and intellectual, but since he is basically a goofball, he often plays the part of the comic handsome guy. His role is to stop Kaine, who runs ahead alone. He is a rich family's young master, but he rebelled against that and entered the Astronaut Academy. However, thanks to the environment he grew up in, he can handle social pleasantries properly and is skilled with ladies, and he also shows off his dandy side, being fussy about food.
uncertain: 'Comic handsome guy' for [jp] (a handsome man who plays the clown).

pilots.en: One of the refugees aboard the transport ship Idaho. Her pensive eyes have a maturity that hardly seems that of a 16-year-old. But that is natural: she has a major secret and has been living with a thorn in her heart. She stubbornly refuses Kaine's ardent advances at first, but gradually opens her heart. Her knowledge of electronics is also considerable.

A 16-year-old refugee girl who was aboard the transport ship Idaho. She is traveling with Linda to look for her parents, from whom she was separated on the Moon. She is full of energy and cheerful, the type who naturally soothes those around her. As the only ordinary person among the three heroines, her ordinariness conversely shone. She quickly entered a steady relationship with Tapp.

Dr. Izumi's granddaughter and the sub-pilot of the Galva FX-II. In the early days she wore a flight cap with goggles when sortieing, but before long she went without a helmet. She calls Kazuya, who was raised with her like a brother, "Big Brother," and has feelings for him, but she realizes Kazuya's feelings for Erika and steps aside. A tomboy who learns karate like Kazuya, she has black-belt-level skill. Also, perhaps because of Dr. Izumi's influence, she is good at tinkering with machines, and once built a see-through camera. When she gets excited or troubled, she has a strange habit of imitating a dog by saying "Uu~, woof!"

The person in charge of Daimobic. He is a father-substitute to Kazuya and his karate teacher. He has also displayed karate techniques such as flying kicks and body strikes, with the "Swallow Double Kick" as his specialty. He has a strong sense of justice and is humane, and is highly respected. It is also thanks to Dr. Izumi that Daimobic can fight on its own judgment without being at the beck and call of Commander Miwa, even though Daimobic receives subsidies from the government. He is a first-rate scientist as well, and often holds the key to a turnaround, such as manufacturing the Photon Missile when he felt threatened by the appearance of the Cobrado, and using the power of Daimolite to change Daimos into a pure energy state. However, he loves sweets, and since he sometimes directed battles while licking a lollipop, I cannot help feeling that his dignity was somewhat lacking. In episode 30, "Danger! Dr. Izumi's Life," he was badly injured trying to protect the Daimolite storehouse and was implanted with an artificial cerebellum made by Baam.
uncertain: 'Cobrado' ([jp]) is a Baam command ship per ja Wikipedia; romanized from kana.
The 'I cannot help feeling' comment is the writer's own voice in the Japanese.
Episode 30 title translated by me ('Danger! Dr. Izumi's Life').

pilots.en: The daughter of the late Grand Marshal Leon and the sister of Admiral Richter. She had gone to the front lines as a budding doctor to treat soldiers, but the battle saucer she was riding was shot down, and she lost her memory from the shock; Kazuya rescued her and they fell in love. After regaining her memory, she leaves Daimobic, but is confined in the Undersea Castle, and as she is about to be executed for treason, she escapes with the help of her mentor, Hospital Director Worin. After that, too, she is toyed with by a strange fate, drifting from place to place and repeatedly missing her beloved Kazuya. After becoming the new leader of the liberation organization, she resolves to fight for peace by a method different from Kazuya's, and becomes a star of hope for both Baam people who wish for peace and Earth activists. She was originally a woman with the triple qualities of being strong, gentle and beautiful, but her love with Kazuya made her grow greatly in spirit.
uncertain: 'Grand Marshal' for [jp] (English Wikipedia says 'Emperor Leon').

pilots.en: Erika's nursemaid. She calls Erika "Ohiisama" (my little princess). Because the late Grand Marshal Leon had asked her to look after the futures of the two siblings, she was one of the few people who could admonish Richter inside the Undersea Demon Castle. She has not aged in vain, and noticed the relationship between Erika and Kazuya right away. She kept supporting Erika and Kazuya's relationship, and for that she was charged with treason, had her wings cut off and was made to do forced labor. After being rescued by the Liberation Army, she became a pillar of support as the guardian of Erika, who had become the new leader.
uncertain: 'Ohiisama' kept in romanization with a gloss.

pilots.en: The pilot of the Galva FX-II and a maxim enthusiast. A close friend of Kazuya, with whom he served aboard Space Daimobic. He plays the cool nihilist, but has a strong sense of justice and cannot be stopped once he flares up. He says spiteful things to Kazuya at every turn, but there are signs that he says them to spur Kazuya on. He grew up in France, and after losing his mother in early childhood he was taken in by his grandfather, Ittosai Yuzuki, and had swordsmanship drilled into him, so his sword skill is first-rate. He is a cautious man who never lets go of the sword on his back, whatever the situation. But he seems to be bad with women, and keeps his distance on the principle that "a wise man does not approach danger." His glasses are for show, but his head is not for show, and his hairstyle has been the same since childhood.
uncertain: 'Ittosai Yuzuki' romanized from kana.

pilots.en: The pilot of Daimos and a karate master. A former astronaut who brought Daimolite back aboard Space Daimobic, dispatched by the International Space Agency. Because his father was posted to the Moon base when he was five, he was raised with Dr. Izumi as a surrogate parent, and was taught karate and shooting. After returning to Earth, he belongs to the Daimobic base, and following his father's last wishes he becomes Daimos's pilot and fights the Baam Earth conquest army. He has a straightforward personality and the stubbornness to stick to his own convictions. In an accident during astronaut training he was left completely paralyzed and once almost gave up on his dream, but he has a past of recovering through bloody effort, and his mental strength is guaranteed. He comes to love the amnesiac girl Erika, and that love will in time lead the universe to peace. His hobby of playing drums is at a professional level. Also, there is data that he tends his hair only once every 36 days.
uncertain: 'International Space Agency' ([jp]) is my translation.

pilots.en: A member of the Koplander Team. She has precognitive ability and the ability to hear Raideen's inner voice, so she gives Akira and the others advice that only she can give. She is a wise and calm woman, the opposite of Mari, and Mari always suspected her relationship with Akira. In the past, in search of something to live for and something to be absorbed in, she was also a member of a biker gang.

Akira's classmate and the idol of Rinkai Gakuen. She is the daughter of Director Higashiyama of the Future Engineering Research Institute, with a cheerful, tomboyish personality, and Akira often teased her about how scatterbrained she was. She becomes a pillar of support for the fighting Akira, and in the end, with the sole wish of helping Akira, joins the Koplander Team and backs up Raideen in Bluger.

The director of the Future Engineering Research Institute and the father of Mari Sakurano. To counter the invasion of the Demon Empire, he built the science fortress Mutropolis. While directing it, he formed the Koplander Team to back up Raideen.

A sporty boy who serves as captain of the soccer club at Rinkai Gakuen. He is destined to become one (fade-in) with Raideen, the legacy of King Ra Mu. To prevent the arrival of the Age of Demons, he fights the Demon Empire with Raideen. He is a hot-blooded man of justice with a cheerful personality, and has the strength not to lose to his own destiny and the courage not to flinch even in desperate situations.
uncertain: 'King Ra Mu' here vs. 'emperor' in the Raideen unit entry (the source wording differs: [jp] vs [jp]).
'Age of Demons' for [jp].

pilots.en: Akira's father and an archaeologist. In the original story, in episode 1 he is turned to stone along with the ship he was on by the Demon forces, and later falls into Sharkin's hands.

Akira's mother, who is missing. In truth she is Princess Lemuria of the ancient Mu Empire. To prevent the revival of the Great Demon Emperor Barao and his ambitions, she had fallen into a twelve-thousand-year sleep. Awakening in the present day, she married Ichiro Hibiki and gave birth to Akira, then disappeared to search for the Star of Ra Mu, the secret treasure of the Mu Empire.

The commander of the Earth Defense Force Pacific Regional Headquarters, who also serves concurrently as Japan's chief of national defense. He is, above all, a belligerent man who thinks a few sacrifices are unavoidable in order to win battles. He seems to want to become a hero, and in order to produce results he attacks indiscriminately, including civilians, and tortures prisoners. A born militarist who declares that civilians are noncombatants and so are a burden, useless mouths to feed, and lower than dogs. He believes all Baam people should be exterminated, and dislikes Kazuya, who shields Erika. He also has a hysterical side, immediately hurling discriminatory words at anyone who does not follow his wishes. In the end, he is arrested on charges of repeatedly ignoring orders from the military's upper echelons.
uncertain: 'Chief of national defense' for [jp] (could be 'Minister of Defense').
Name order: Sakimori (given) Miwa (family).
